articles.title: Researchers warned of North Korean hacking tactics years before record $6.3B Binance heist | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Cybersecurity experts have long warned of the persistent and patient threat from North Korea's long-running hacks. The world's largest crypto exchange was still caught off-guard.
articles.body_text: Crypto giant Binance says North Korean hackers used fake social media profiles and the lure of a potential job offer as part of a months-long scheme aimed at tricking an employee into downloading malicious software onto their laptop. Researchers have repeatedly warned about long-running social engineering attacks that can go on for months. This latest attack allowed the hackers to patiently worm their way into Binance’s systems to steal a record $6.3 billion in crypto last week, the company has now confirmed. The hack, disclosed in an updated statement posted on X on Tuesday, prompted the world’s largest crypto exchange to suspend customer withdrawals across its network. The FBI and blockchain investigators have blamed North Korea for the heist. The country has been long accused of carrying out massive cryptocurrency thefts in recent years to fund its internationally sanctioned nuclear weapons program. In its latest statement, Binance said that North Korean hackers, posing as recruiters hiring for a job, contacted a software engineer who works on wallets at the company. Following two interviews with the purported company, the engineer was instructed to download an apparent coding assignment as part of the interview process. When opened, the assignment contained malicious code that compromised the engineer’s work-issued laptop. Binance said its security tools did not detect the malware. That foothold in Binance’s network allowed the hackers to access an internal tool capable of taking over the work computers of two other engineers on the wallet team. One of those engineers had unwittingly downloaded a tampered app containing password-stealing malware months earlier after searching for the software in search engine results. While Binance replaced that compromised engineer’s laptop, the hackers used the engineer’s stolen credentials to break into the computer of a third engineer, whose job allowed them access to systems capable of controlling billions of dollars in crypto. Binance said the attack “should not have happened,” and that it had improved its network security following the theft. The hack underscores an ongoing tactic in the North Korean regime’s repertoire of attacks targeting the crypto industry and high-net worth individuals. Researchers have warned for years that North Korean hackers pose as venture capitalists, investors, and recruiters using dossiers of stolen American identities to trick employees into granting access to their systems. These attacks are widely known across the crypto industry and have been the subject of repeated warnings from the U.S. government and cybersecurity giants in recent years. Some half of all intrusions at U.S. tech companies last year were attributed to North Koreans posing as remote IT workers and fake recruiters. By Binance’s own account, the company faced at least 57 suspected attacks from North Korea, which it said reflect the “persistent threat posed by state-sponsored actors targeting the cryptocurrency industry.” But how the hackers were able to convince the engineer into downloading malware given the highly publicized threat, and bypass security weaknesses in Binance’s own network, will likely be the focus of investigators’ attention. While the case exposes how North Korean hackers use social engineering, such as offers of employment, to trick employees into granting access to their systems, it’s ultimately the responsibility of the company to ensure its systems cannot run unauthorized or untrusted software that could cause a compromise.

articles.summary: The five-year-old startup raised a $1.3 billion round led by Bessemer.
articles.body_text: Fal , a San Francisco-based startup that hosts and runs AI video, image, and audio models, has raised $1.3 billion in its latest funding round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Nvidia, Sound Ventures, and T. Rowe Price. The deal values Fal at $16 billion, double its $8 billion valuation in April, Bloomberg reported . The startup announced its Series E and F rounds at the same time, noting that a combined $1.65 billion was raised across both. (Sequoia led the earlier round.) Fal surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue earlier this year, Bloomberg’s report noted. Companies providing inference services, including Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Modal, have also been growing rapidly and raising large funding rounds at higher valuations . But their gross margins remain thin because of the high cost of buying or leasing compute, according to several people familiar with inference companies’ financials. Fal was co-founded in 2021 by Burkay Gur, a former Coinbase machine learning leader and Oracle engineer, and Gorkem Yurtseven, who was previously a developer at Amazon. articles.title: Reddit tests ads in search results as traffic declines and growth concerns mount | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The new ad placements could help Reddit squeeze more revenue from existing users as Google's AI search changes how people discover its content.
articles.body_text: Just days after warning investors about declining search traffic and a weaker-than-expected revenue forecast, Reddit is looking for more ways to make money from its existing users. On Tuesday, the company announced that it’s beginning to test ad placements in its search results pages, allowing advertisers to reach users as they search for products, recommendations, and other information on its platform. “Ads in search may appear based on a range of factors, including contextual relevance to a user’s search query,” Reddit shared in its announcement about the new ad placements. “This is an initial test with a select group of eligible advertisers. During this test, we will evaluate and understand how users respond to these ads so we can refine the experience for users and advertisers over time.” The company offered examples of what sort of ads might appear, suggesting that a search for “espresso station” might display ads for espresso machines, coffee, or mugs, while a search for “home office setup” could surface ads for things like monitors, desks, and office chairs. The ad test comes at a time when Reddit is reckoning with how AI has been changing the web’s landscape, and subsequently its reach. Despite beating Wall Street’s estimates for revenue and earnings per share, the company’s stock dropped after it reported its third-quarter results last week , with fourth-quarter guidance that predicted sales of $1 billion to $1.03 billion, below expectations of $1.05 billion. This was tied to Reddit’s declining search traffic referrals resulting from Google’s move to an AI-powered search experience. AI search now sends less traffic to publishers’ websites, as features like AI Mode provide answers directly on Google’s Search Result pages, reducing clicks to other websites. Reddit also said that its global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in the quarter, and were down 2% year-over-year. The company noted that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low double-digit percentage by the fourth quarter. This leaves the company needing to earn more revenue from its existing users, which is where these new ads come in. The ads could prove to be more valuable to Reddit after it makes its planned shift to a logged-in experience, which was also announced during earnings. The company said it will make the transition gradually, initially in markets outside the U.S. The decision to limit its content to logged-in users serves multiple purposes — it protects Reddit’s site from unauthorized AI scraping, and it increases its value to advertisers. Logged-in users are worth more to advertisers because they provide additional signals about their interests and behavior, allowing for better-targeted, more profitable ads. articles.title: Ten years later, 'Pokémon Go to the polls' still haunts the internet | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Hillary Clinton's 2016 political gaffe has become an irony-shrouded rallying cry for jaded young voters who still dare to hope for change.
articles.body_text: In the lead-up to a presidential election that would irrefutably transform American culture, Hillary Clinton took the stage at a rally in Virginia as she campaigned to become the first female president. “We’re going to have a lot of jobs — jobs from building infrastructure to coding. Creating new apps,” she said. “I don’t know who created Pokémon GO, but I’m trying to figure out how we get them to have Pokémon Go to the polls .” Ten years later, it is once again Election Day in the United States. Now, most app developers aren’t even writing their own code anymore, thanks to AI, and Pokémon GO has been sold to a company wholly owned by Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. The only thing about that political moment that hasn’t changed is that “Pokémon Go to the polls” memes still crop up on every Election Day. “It was very bold and confident, and also just sounded so terribly out of touch and corny,” Cesar Ruiz de Castilla, an elected ward committee member in Philadelphia, told TechCrunch. “I don’t know if the mainstream media cared that much about it, but everyone was making a meme about it and talking about it online.” Since then, digital culture has become increasingly inextricable from the fate of American politics. Donald Trump tweeted his way through his first term, then later started his own social media platform ; presidential campaigns hire meme managers ; the White House invites podcasters and content creators to press briefings; Elon Musk even spun up his own advisory group under Trump that named itself after the cutesy doge meme and then slashed international aid programs. “The 2016 election was such a monumental moment in internet history, and we were all there for it — our politics have become more, not just divided, but segmented online,” Organizer Memes , a political influencer who teaches Gen Z activists how to reach their peers online via memes, told TechCrunch. “It’s a relic of an optimistic, bygone political era.” Now, people who weren’t even old enough to vote in 2016 reflect on the year as a cultural turning point, even calling it “ the last good year .” It’s a sentiment that isn’t so much political as it is rooted in nostalgia for an era of internet culture before AI slop, when we used social media to connect with friends, rather than doomscrolling through an algorithmic feed of people we don’t even follow. At the start of the new year, this yearning for the old internet became a viral sentiment as millions of people shared throwback photos from 2016 on Instagram. Spotify reported that user-generated playlists featuring 2016 in their titles spiked 790% in the first three weeks of the year, and the company changed its Instagram bio at the time to say it’s “romanticizing 2016 again.” Never mind that, at the time, the internet perceived 2016 as a cursed year, even before the election — months earlier, one Slate columnist wondered how 2016 compared to 1348, the year the Black Death took hold in Europe. “[Pokémon Go to the polls] is in that era of the singular internet, when Facebook and Twitter and Tumblr were all kind of bouncing content back-and-forth and not just this complete anarchic mess of 25 platforms that we now have and don’t use,” Organizer Memes said. Organizer Memes also notes that some cultural touchstones that felt more significant then — like the obsession with Harambe the gorilla — haven’t had as much staying power as “Pokémon Go to the polls.”

articles.title: CrowdStrike to shell out nearly $500M for 2 AI security startups as the market for securing agents takes off | TechCrunch
articles.summary: CrowdStrike said it will buy Fiddler AI, which makes AI agent observability software, and Dreadnode, which helps companies automate AI security testing.
articles.body_text: Cybersecurity giant CrowdStrike is buying two AI security companies that expand its products to more broadly monitor, test, and cover AI models and agents, as companies across industries start rolling out AI agents and models wholesale. CrowdStrike said it will buy Fiddler AI , which makes observability software for monitoring AI agents inside enterprises, and Dreadnode , which helps companies automate security testing specifically aimed at detecting flaws in AI models, apps, and agents before they are set live. The company is paying around $400 million for Fiddler AI, and about $95 million for Dreadnode, according to The Wall Street Journal . The deals are happening at a time of significant upheaval in the cybersecurity space, especially as companies’ policies and processes lag behind AI adoption within their walls. Teams and individual employees alike are experimenting with AI tools, automating workflows, vibe-coding custom apps, and deploying armies of AI agents to do their bidding, which is understandably causing headaches for security teams. CrowdStrike, whose products are used widely across enterprises and governments, is clearly trying to leverage its already significant heft and presence to capture a share of this quickly burgeoning market . It’s not alone, of course, as we’ve already seen several startups and cybersecurity vendors raising dozens of millions in funding to solve issues for companies, though most of these approaches are essentially based on the conviction that existing security software isn’t enough to monitor and control AI tools, connectors, or usage. The company has itself been building detection and response controls , dubbed Falcon Guardian, to help companies see and understand what agents are doing on their devices, and these acquisitions seem to further flesh out its offerings. Fiddler AI is going to be part of CrowdStrike’s Falcon platform as Falcon Observe, where it’ll ostensibly help the company’s clients evaluate agents before they’re deployed, understand their actions, and monitor what they do, and feed that information as telemetry into the broader platform. Dreadnode, meanwhile, will be integrated into the Falcon Guardian product , to which the startup’s software will feed its testing results as security policy recommendations. Founded in 2018, Fiddler AI has raised a total of about $99 million to date, according to PitchBook. Dreadnode, founded in 2023, has raised $14 million so far. articles.title: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute | TechCrunch
articles.summary: At a moment when Anthropic's compute margins should be getting better, they’re getting worse.
articles.body_text: There’s a lot of mystery around the finances of major AI labs, and as Anthropic inches towards it IPO, we’re starting to get some answers. In particular, the company is finally disclosing more about the economics of compute, and how much of Anthropic’s skyrocketing revenue is being lost to compute costs. In a new filing on Monday , Anthropic released data that showed those margins on compute actually getting worse. The filing was an update to the S-1 released last week — but where that filing’s financial disclosures only covered through June 30 of this year, the new data extended to disclose results through an extra quarter, to September 30. Broadly, Anthropic had a good quarter: revenue reached $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion in the previous quarter, suggesting durable growth. But the operating loss grew at the same time, thanks in large part to growing compute costs. Looking at the compute margins makes the picture even worse. In the new quarter, compute took up 58% of the company’s revenue, up from 48% the quarter before. At a moment when the company could win over IPO investors by showing margins improving, they’re getting worse. A chart in the filing shows this even more clearly, tracking the company’s revenue for every dollar spent on compute. Since the start of 2025, it’s been steadily growing, peaking at just over 2x this past quarter, then falling back down to 1.72x. Many indications imply that this shift in compute margins is more of a blip than a long-term problem, but it still tells us important things about the business of running a major lab. Trying to keep up with demand, Anthropic’s compute bill shot up to $10 billion for the quarter, including, as the filing notes, “$5.0 billion of compute under short-term commitments, which currently costs significantly more than comparable compute procured under our multi-year commitments.” Basically, demand was growing so fast that Anthropic had to scramble for compute, which meant paying higher rates. Some of those deals have already played out in public. Anthropic has been paying SpaceX $1.25 billion a month for compute, alongside multibillion-dollar deals with Nscale , Akamai , and Volta . In the parlance of the industry, these are neoclouds rather than hyperscalers — smaller outfits that offer more flexible compute deals at higher rates. Anthropic’s margins got worse in Q3 because of deals like these, and there’s no sign they’ll be able to do without them anytime soon. As the new filing puts it, “We expect compute and infrastructure expenses to increase in absolute dollars and remain our largest operating expense for the foreseeable future as additional committed compute becomes available to us under multi-year arrangements with CSPs, and as we continue to invest in additional compute.” Anthropic is still trying to lower its compute costs. In particular, the company talks quite a bit about its efforts to build its own compute base under a project it calls “Anthropic Direct.” But with demand growing so fast, those efforts aren’t going to be able to keep pace, and the neoclouds will continue to be the best option they have. In a sense, these are champagne problems. As long as revenue is growing at nearly 50% a quarter, few investors will worry about high compute costs — and the moment demand slows down, investors may be comforted by a compute picture that has gotten a lot sunnier. But it’s a reminder of how much AI labs still depend on the trillion-dollar infrastructure buildout — and how vulnerable they are to hiccups in that process. It’s easy to imagine the data center buildout slowing down over the next year if bond markets get skittish or local opposition gets more intense. There’s not much Anthropic can do to address either of those risks, and either one would make a messy compute picture a whole lot messier. In the meantime, the future of Anthropic and other labs will be at the mercy of compute prices. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . articles.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Apple's new App Store rules will require 18+ ratings for dating apps and AI companions that offer sexual or romantic content.
articles.body_text: Apple is adjusting its App Store policies to make it more difficult for minors to use online dating apps or AI companions that engage in “sexual or romantic content,” the tech giant shared in an announcement to developers on Monday. The new rules follow other changes the company has made to better protect minors, which include the rollout of its age assurance technology globally and more parental controls and child safety features . While most major dating services typically restrict their platform to adults, Apple’s new policy will require all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features to carry an 18+ rating. Starting November 16, developers will be required to include new content descriptors to ensure their app’s age ratings reflect its features, the company said. It’s perhaps more interesting how this rule could impact AI companion apps, or those where such functionality is one of many features. Often targeted at younger people, Character.AI, Replika, and other AI apps let people create AI companions, including friends, lovers, boyfriends and girlfriends, and other fantasy characters. xAI last year also launched 3D animated AI companions that allowed users to unlock NSFW capabilities . As of last summer, top AI companion apps across the Apple App Store and Google Play had been downloaded 220 million times globally . The company noted that in Brazil, apps that provide location-sharing features for families can request an official rating from the government’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security (MJSP/Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública), instead of being required to list them with the A16 rating, as the local law requires. articles.title: The Cybertruck made a mark but missed its moment
articles.summary: Tesla is finally delivering the long-delayed Cybertruck, but the polarizing EV may have already missed its moment to launch the company into its next phase.
articles.body_text: It feels like a thousand years since Tesla first introduced the Cybertruck, but it’s actually only been about a thousand days. Still, that’s a long time in the auto world, and to say people are getting antsy waiting would be a huge understatement. The Cybertruck certainly took its time getting here, slogging its way through a global pandemic, a presidential election, two ongoing wars, and many other terrible things that have happened over the past four years. Tesla CEO Elon Musk’s acquisition of Twitter and his emergence as a “haver of bad opinions, especially about Jews” also took place within this time and is sure to cast a shadow over the Cybertruck’s big moment. Now, with the first few Cybertrucks poised to finally reach a small handful of customers this week, Tesla is facing a much different world than it did in 2019 — a world of plummeting profit margins, rising interest rates, dwindling market share, and a loss in investor confidence that Tesla was poised to take over the world. Musk’s recent scandals have metastasized and folded back over themselves to the point where they’ve become an indecipherable rat king of bad news that most people would prefer to tune out. If Tesla thinks the Cybertruck will help turn things around, it’s probably mistaken. When it was first announced, there were no electric trucks on the market. Now, there are at least three… and more on the way. The Cybertruck arrives at a time when the EV market is cooling, as first adopters give way to bargain-hunters who are coming up empty. Experts say what we really need to drive adoption is a mass-market EV that’s affordable and practical. The Cybertruck is neither. It stands proudly as the antithesis of what the market needs. Tesla fans are convinced it will change the industry forever. But it’s been over four years, so let’s revisit the history of the world’s weirdest, and quite possibly hardest to build, truck. Pour some CyberBeer into your CyberStein, toss on your Cyber backpack, and get ready for some Cybertruck 101. What is a Cybertruck? If you’ve been in a coma for the last four years (and honestly, I envy you), the Cybertruck was first introduced at a lavish event in November 2019 at Tesla’s design studio in California. It was only the sixth vehicle ever introduced by Tesla, and it was supposed to herald the company’s first effort to capture the big-volume, highly lucrative truck market. But Musk had no interest in turning the highly successful Model 3 into a truck. Instead, he wanted something straight out of Blade Runner. The result? Angular, dystopian, impractical, and depending on who you ask, kind of goofy-looking. The stainless steel body would emphasize every scratch and fingerprint. The misaligned panels were familiar to anyone who’s owned a Tesla. The truck bed couldn’t even hold that much stuff. And the windshield wiper… well, let’s just say it won’t be doing much wiping. Going back and reading our coverage of the actual Cybertruck reveal is a great reminder of how sometimes the first reaction is the most telling. As our then-transportation reporter Sean O’Kane wrote (emphasis mine): > Musk spent months telling everyone that Tesla’s first electric pickup truck would look like something out of Blade Runner. And yet, for a brief moment after the truck appeared onstage, the entire room — one full of Tesla customers and fans from all around the world — fell practically silent in disbelief. > As he rattled off the truck’s specs and features, I heard a few low exclamations of “what the fuck?” before the hooting and hollering picked back up. It was as if the people in the room were expecting a different kind of magic trick, one where Musk would coyly laugh before revealing the true Tesla pickup truck, which would still eat Ford F-150s for breakfast but look a little less alien. (That feeling only seemed to multiply when Tesla chief designer Franz von Holzhausen broke the truck’s windows while trying to demonstrate their durability.) Still, it’s different, and different can be interesting. You can’t deny that the Cybertruck holds a certain appeal, whether as an object of desire or as one of ridicule. People have been flocking to Tesla showrooms to see preproduction models. Social platforms are teaming with “get a load of this truck” videos. People want selfies with the Cybertruck. But do they want the truck itself? Spectacle doesn’t necessarily translate into sales. Ed Niedermeyer, author of Ludicrous: The Unvarnished Story of Tesla Motors, dismissed the Cybertruck as a “meme” vehicle in a recent episode of his podcast, Autonocast. His co-host Alex Roy predicted it will be a huge win for Tesla. The truth may lie somewhere in the middle. Much will depend on Tesla’s ability to transform its millions of reservation holders into actual owners. How much will it cost? We still don’t know. In 2019, Tesla said it would make three versions of the Cybertruck: * Single motor rear-wheel drive with 250 miles of range, 7,500-pound towing capacity, and zero to 60mph capabilities in under 6.5 seconds for $39,900 * Dual motor all-wheel drive with 300 miles of range, 10,000-pound towing capacity, and zero to 60mph in under 4.5 seconds for $49,900 * Triple motor all-wheel drive with 500 miles of range, 14,000-pound towing capacity, and zero to 60mph in under 2.9 seconds for $69,900. Those were the 2019 prices. If the company announces new prices on November 30th, they will most assuredly be higher. The single-motor version, for example, is predicted to retail for over $50,000, while the tri-motor version will likely be over $80,000. Tesla has slashed prices on its Model 3 and Y vehicles this past year, but the Cybertruck seems destined for the premium category. And that could determine whether this is a truck for regular people or a plaything for the rich. Production was originally supposed to start in late 2021. But by August 2021, the company announced a delay until 2022 — and then later to “hopefully” 2023. In the meantime, competitors like Ford and Rivian have launched their own electric pickups, with Ford saying that it plans to make 150,000 F-150 Lightnings this year. “An angry triangle” Finding a measured opinion on the Cybertruck is a bit of a wild goose chase. This is a truck that stirs people’s passions. You either love it or you hate it. There’s no in-between. Car designers who spoke to Business Insider called it “crude” or “a child’s toy.” Others were less charitable. Car designer Adrian Clarke described the Cybertruck as “a low polygon joke that only exists in the fever dreams of Tesla fans that stands high on the smell of Elon Musk’s flatulences.” Others just ripped on it for being an “angry triangle.” Giorgetto Giugiaro, the legendary car designer behind the Lotus Esprit, BMW M1, and most notably, the DeLorean DMC-12, told NPR that he doesn’t want to judge the Cybertruck “as beautiful or ugly. It certainly has its admirers who want a vehicle to stand out.” But the panel gaps aside, production-ready versions of the Cybertruck aren’t without their defenders. The Autopian’s Dave Tracy saw a version in a Tesla showroom and came away impressed, calling it better than the prototypes that were drawing the most ire and “badass.” The matte black version that Franz von Holzhausen drove to a recent Malibu cars and coffee event drew the most ire. The panel gaps were especially pronounced, while other aspects appeared slapdash and poorly thought out. Car journalist Daniel Golson, who saw it in person, was flabbergasted in his report to Jalopnik: > I’ve been around hundreds of prototype cars in my career, ranging from early test mules to near-production prototypes, and I’ve never seen an automaker proudly present something of this poor quality, especially not this late in development. Much has been written about the use of stainless steel for the exterior as the main source of the production delays. Steel is incredibly difficult to bend and manipulate, which complicates Tesla’s ability to shape it into body panels that line up correctly and don’t result in huge gaps. It’s also nearly impossible to flatten and has a tendency to spring back into its curved form. This is why it’s rarely used in vehicle manufacturing. It’s too tough, too expensive, and too heavy than other, more traditional materials. Musk’s demands for an exterior that was also bulletproof drove Tesla to seek out thicker steel than what is typically used in the auto industry. This made it more difficult to form, spurring much of the production calamities, according to The Wall Street Journal. Musk himself has been blunt in his characterization of the Cybertruck. The truck will be a huge manufacturing challenge for Tesla, he said in an internal memo reported by CNBC over the summer. He also said he was worried about “precision” in manufacturing the truck because its “straight edges” mean variations show up “like a sore thumb.” “We dug our own grave with the Cybertruck,” Musk said later in an earnings call. “Cybertruck’s one of those special products that comes along only once in a long while. And special products that come along once in a long while are just incredibly difficult to bring to market to reach volume, to be prosperous.” Tesla’s future won’t hinge on the Cybertruck Martin Viecha, head of Tesla investor relations, recently tweeted that Tesla is “between two major growth waves.” The first wave started with the release of the Model 3 in 2017 and continues with the Model Y in 2020. The next one “will be driven by the next gen vehicle,” Viecha said. The Cybertruck doesn’t enter into that calculation because Tesla doesn’t expect to make that many, at least not at first. In that “we dug our own grave” earnings call, Musk also said he wanted to “temper expectations” for the truck, adding the company could face “enormous challenges” in ramping up production and making it cash flow positive. He said that Tesla is targeting an annual run rate (the number of vehicles it plans to make in a year) of 250,000 for the Cybertruck, but it’s not likely to hit that output until 2025 at the earliest. The Cybertruck is set to arrive at an unsettled time for Tesla. The company’s once eye-watering sales growth has since leveled off as it deals with stiffer competition in the EV space. Some investors are counting on the truck to spark renewed interest in Tesla, especially at a time when Musk’s online shenanigans are a drag on the brand’s reputation. A successful Cybertruck launch “will prove to the doubters that Musk can successfully expand the Tesla halo effect as more consumers head down the EV path over the coming years,” said Wedbush’s Dan Ives in a recent research note. Not everyone agrees. Jefferies analyst Philippe Houchois said Tesla is better off shelving the Cybertruck in the interest of getting its number back up. “However unlikely just a few days before first deliveries, canceling Cybertruck would probably be positive for shares,” Houchois wrote last week. “With 2024 already a lost year for growth, it would help Tesla refocus on an edge that was built on simplicity, scale and speed.” And Morgan Stanley’s Adam Jonas said Tesla should focus on new software products that it can license to other automakers, like Full Self-Driving, which is anticipated to shed its “beta” status as part of the Cybertruck delivery event. No one asked for this I’ve been covering Tesla a long time, and I’ve learned never to bet against Musk’s ability to pull a rabbit out of his hat. That said, a stainless steel electric truck that upends manufacturing norms and subverts customer expectations about what a truck should look like was always going to be a tall order. There have been bad-looking trucks before. Arguably, the current design trend of massive trucks with overly tall, flat front ends is extremely shitty — and not just for the pedestrians who stand a much better chance of being crushed underneath their tires. In the long history of trucks — from the 1925 Model T Roadster to today’s hulking, flat-nosed behemoths — it’s reasonable to assume that we have not seen anything remotely like the Tesla Cybertruck. No one was asking for it, and yet, this week, 10 people are reportedly slated to receive the first Cybertrucks. A big day for all of those who care about the Cybertruck. articles.title: Hotet från Trumps man på valdagen: ”Kommer jaga er”
articles.summary: Donald Trumps administration försöker påverka valprocessen ända in över mållinjen. På valdagen fortsätter påståendena om olagliga röster. ”Vi kommer att jaga er”, skriver Markwayne Mullin, minister för inrikes säkerhet, på X.
articles.body_text: Donald Trumps administration försöker påverka valprocessen ända in över mållinjen. På valdagen fortsätter påståendena om olagliga röster. ”Vi kommer att jaga er”, skriver Markwayne Mullin, minister för inrikes säkerhet, på X. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Donald Trump har upprepat påståendena om utländska medborgare som röstar till förbannelse. Ända fram till valdagen har en juridisk strid pågått med Kalifornien om att de ska rensa ut 20 000 ”misstänkta” namn på vallistorna, eftersom de menar att det sannolikt handlar om utländska medborgare. De har inte presenterat några bevis och liknande listor har tidigare visat sig vara luftslott. På måndagen stoppades försöket återigen i domstol. Det hindrar inte att liknande påståenden fortsätter in över mållinjen. ”Valdagen är i morgon. Justitiedepartementet förväntar sig att alla federala vallagar följs. Har du tips om olaglig verksamhet, bland annat att personer utan medborgarskap röstar, dubbelröstning eller att falska röster stoppas in i valurnor, kontakta FBI” , skrev justitieminister Todd Blanche på X sent på måndagen. ”De som bryter mot lagen kommer att hittas och åtalas” , fortsätter han. På valdagen passar Markwayne Mullin, minister för inrikes säkerhet, på att leverera ytterligare ett hot. ”Om du röstar olagligt i det här landet och INTE har rösträtt kommer departementet för inrikes säkerhet att hitta dig, jaga dig, och du kommer att ställas inför rätta och straffas så hårt som lagen tillåter. Bara amerikanska medborgare ska avgöra amerikanska val” , skriver han. James Percival, chefsjurist vid samma departement uppmanar också människor att anmäla valfusk.

articles.body_text: Kronofogden har sålt en nazistskylt på auktion för tusentals kronor. Historikern Nils Exner är rädd att den ska hamna i fel händer. – Bara för några veckor sedan, i Kalmar, hittade de massvis med vapen och naziföremål i en privatpersons hus, säger han. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. En minst sagt udda skylt har auktionerats ut på uppdrag av Kronofogden . ”Deutches Konsulat” är skrivet på den. Under texten syns Nazitysklands emblem med en örn och en svastika. Den hängde vid det tyska konsulatet i Stockholm. Det vinnande budet blev 50 000 kronor och lades av en privatperson. Historikern Nils Exner arbetar för Humboldtuniversitetet i Berlin och har forskat på andra världskriget. Han blev överraskad när han såg försäljningen. – Jag tycker att det är intressant att en Svensk myndighet samlar in pengar genom att sälja nationalsocialistiska föremål, säger han. Han menar att de som säljer nazistiska föremål måste säkerställa att de hamnar i ansvarsfulla händer. – Det är stor skillnad på om de används för att lära folk om nazismen på ett museum eller om de hamnar hos en privatperson som hyllar nazism, säger Exner. Han pekar på att föremålen ofta används i fel syften när de hamnar hos privatpersoner.

articles.title: ”Så trött på alla som kysser Trump där bak”
articles.summary: Människorna strömmar ut från Jeepfabriken utanför Detroit efter morgonskiftet. Här vann Trump stort i presidentvalet senast, men krig, höga bensinpriser och tunna orderingångar gör honom till ett sänke i valet. Väljarna i Michigan kan ha avgörandet i sina händer.
articles.body_text: Människorna strömmar ut från Jeepfabriken utanför Detroit efter morgonskiftet. Här vann Trump stort i presidentvalet senast, men krig, höga bensinpriser och tunna orderingångar gör honom till ett sänke i valet. Väljarna i Michigan kan ha avgörandet i sina händer. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Klockan är efter två på eftermiddagen och det tidiga skiftet har stämplat ut. Arbetarna kommer släntrande mot parkeringen i Warren, strax nordost om centrala Detroit. Stellantis fabrik här är enorm – fasaderna fortsätter i hundratals meter och den totala golvytan motsvarar 40 fotbollsplaner. Man har byggt bilar här i 90 år. Då var det Dodge, nu är det mest Jeep Wagoneer. Man har den större Grand Wagoneer på programmet också, men den är så kall bland kunderna att arbetarna som pratar med Expressen inte är säkra på om de faktiskt tillverkar så många. Det är därför det inte går lika mycket folk åt andra hållet. På grund av orderingången är eftermiddagsskiftet nerskuret till en skärva av sin gamla storlek. Regnet hänger i luften. Att betrakta det här är som att stå i en Springsteenlåt. ”The big three”, de tre stora bilföretagen Ford, GM och Stellantis (det som var Chrysler förr) och resten av bilindustrin står för 20 procent av jobben i Michigan. För Donald Trump har det här varit typexemplet på vad som ska göras great i Amerika igen – mer tillverkning, mer industri, mer amerikanska varor. Men tullarna han infört har gjort tillvaron osäker för biltillverkarna i USA, inte minst här i Detroitområdet där bilindustrin är så tätt sammanvävd med fabrikerna på kanadensiska sidan att att bildelar korsar gränsen upp till åtta gånger innan de sitter i en färdig bil. Bara en av fyra tillfrågade i Michigan tyckte att man fått det bättre under Trump, enligt en undersökning från Washington Post i september.

articles.title: Carolines son handlade för 60 000 kronor på Roblox
articles.summary: Bara några dagar in på semestern upptäckte Caroline Damberg att hennes konto var tomt. Hennes son hade lyckats göra köp för 60 000 kronor i spelet Roblox. – Hur är det ens möjligt?
articles.body_text: Bara några dagar in på semestern upptäckte Caroline Damberg att hennes konto var tomt. Hennes son hade lyckats göra köp för 60 000 kronor i spelet Roblox. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Caroline Damberg hade nästan 60 000 kronor på banken i början av juni 2026. Pengarna skulle gå till att reparera bilen senare under månaden. När hon två veckor senare skulle betala i kassan gick köpet inte igenom. – Jag går in på mitt konto och ser att alla pengar är borta. Hennes första tanke var att hon hade utsatts för ett bedrägeri. Men när hon gick igenom sitt bankkonto hemma upptäckte hon att pengarna har gått till köp i spelet Roblox . Hon hade lagt in sina bankuppgifter i spelet under julen för att köpa en julklapp. – Jag trodde att det automatiskt krävdes att man identifierar sig med Bank-ID inför varje köp, säger hon. Men hennes 10-åriga son hade klurat ut hur han ska handla i spelet. – Vissa dagar hade han köpt för över 8 000 kronor. Jag fick en chock, hur är det ens möjligt att han kan sitta och köpa hejvilt utan att någon reagerar? Sonen hade gjort över 150 köp på mellan 9 och 895 kronor. Betalningarna hade gått till Apple. – Apple-kontot är kopplat till hans mejl och köpbekräftelserna har gått dit. Jag har varit riktigt chockad. Hur är det ens möjligt när jag bara har lagt in mitt bankkort en gång?

articles.title: Chatta med Expressen om valet i USA
articles.summary: Johan Eriksson på plats.
articles.body_text: Okej, vi får ta och stänga butiken här för den här gången. Det kommer vara full fart på Expressen.se under natten och morgonen, så håll koll där så får ni allt ni behöver kring valet! I representanthuset är det väldigt, väldigt ovanligt. George Bush gjorde det 2002, Clinton -98 och innan dess Franklin Roosevelt 1934. Senaten är lite mer rörligt, både Trump 2018 och Biden 2022 tog ett par till stolar. Men det vanligaste är helt klart att presidentens parti går bakåt. Det har ju spekulerats i att Trump vill forcera fram en "deal" med Iran genom att ta upp bombningarna, men att han inte velat göra det inför valet för att inte skada republikanernas chanser mer. Väldigt många – på båda sidor – är väldigt trötta på kriget och framför allt på de högra bensin- och dieselpriserna. Om det betyder att han verkligen kommer dra i gång igen? Helst skulle han nog bara hota Iran till underkastelse. Men det har ju inte heller visat sig vara så lätt... Vet inte exakt vilket distrikt du har sett, eller hur stor svängning det var, men jag skulle säga att överlag finns det en större andel nu som är trötta på Trump. Så var det till exempel när jag var i södra Texas häromveckan. Där hade Trump gått fram starkt men nu var det många som ledsnat. https://www.expressen.se/nyheter/varlden/valjarna-som-sviker-trump-angrar-mig/ ...och angående förra frågan, så här är läget i senaten. Tror man att Kalshi har svaret blir det 53 demokrater i senaten.

articles.title: Sju flyg bombhotade på samma dag – experten: ”Kan inte minnas”
articles.summary: Minst sju flygplan utsattes för bombhot under tisdagen. Det är ovanligt att det sker flera incidenter samtidigt, enligt terrorforskaren Magnus Ranstorp. – Jag kan inte minnas att det förekommit tidigare på det sättet.
articles.body_text: Minst sju flygplan utsattes för bombhot under tisdagen. Det är ovanligt att det sker flera incidenter samtidigt, enligt terrorforskaren Magnus Ranstorp. – Jag kan inte minnas att det förekommit tidigare på det sättet. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. SAS-planet hade lyft från Köpenhamn och var på väg mot Warszawa när det utsattes för ett hot i luften. – Kaptenen sade att det hade ringts in ett hot mot planet, sade en passagerare till danska BT. Under tisdagen kom sedan ytterligare bombhot mot sex civila flyg. Alla har bekräftats vara falsklarm, enligt The Guardian . Att bombhot riktas mot flygplan förekommer, enligt terrorforskaren Magnus Ranstorp . – Men inte mot så många plan, i så många olika länder samtidigt. Jag kan inte minnas att det förekommit tidigare på det sättet. Att alla bombhot inträffade samma dag kan tyda på någon slags samordning, säger han. – Man måste dels analysera vilka rutter som blivit måltavlor för detta, vilka flygbolag och vilka länder som förekommer. Det kan finnas flera syften med bombhoten, enligt Ranstorp: dels att sprida rädsla och skräck och dels att se hur myndigheter hanterar händelserna.

articles.title: Kvinna blev påkörd och dog – truckförare misstänks för brott
articles.summary: Kvinnan var på väg hem från jobbet när hon blev påkörd av en truck inne på företaget Alleimas område – och dog. Nu misstänks truckföraren för brott, skriver Dagens Arbete. ”Dödsolyckan var en tragedi”, skriver Annika Molander på Alleima i ett mejl.
articles.body_text: Kvinnan var på väg hem från jobbet när hon blev påkörd av en truck inne på företaget Alleimas område – och dog. Nu misstänks truckföraren för brott, skriver Dagens Arbete. ”Dödsolyckan var en tragedi” , skriver Annika Molander på Alleima i ett mejl. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det var vid 22.30-tiden på kvällen den 5 maj som en kvinna i 50-årsåldern cyklade hemåt efter att ha avslutat sitt arbetspass på Alleima i Sandviken . Då blev hon påkörd av en truck – och dog av sina skador . Enligt Dagens Arbete cyklade hon på cykelbanan längs industriområdets huvudväg när trucken svängde ut. Olyckan utreddes inledningsvis som en arbetsplatsolycka vid Riksenheten för miljö- och arbetsmiljöbrott (Rema). Men i somras avskrevs ärendet, då det enligt Rema inte gick att ”lasta arbetsgivaren” för händelsen. Nu utreds olyckan i stället av allmänna åklagarkammaren i Gävle och mannen som körde trucken är misstänkt för vållande till annans död, skriver Dagens Arbete (DA). – Vi har hållit förhör och delgivit misstanke mot den här personen. Det är han som fört det fordon som uppenbarligen har dödat kvinnan, säger åklagare Micael Dahlberg till tidningen. DA har tagit del av Alleimas egen utredning, och skriver att företaget har kommit fram till att truckföraren sannolikt hade skymd sikt vid olyckan. Dels på grund av truckens last, dels på grund av att det var mörkt och begränsad belysning. För Expressen uppger Alleima att man inte vill kommentera några detaljer eller föregå förundersökningen, men företagets presskontakt Annika Molander skriver i ett mejl att ”dödsolyckan var en tragedi”.

articles.title: Allt om mellanårsvalet: Följ ödesdramat i USA
articles.summary: Följ Expressens direktrapport med senaste nytt om valet.
articles.body_text: Årets mellanårsval är det dyraste i USA:s historia, med över 11 miljarder dollar som har spenderats på politisk reklam. Det rapporterar New York Times. Republikanerna har ett ekonomiskt övertag gentemot Demokraterna, framför allt genom president Trumps förmögenhet – men också att världens rikaste man, Elon Musk, har lagt uppemot en halv miljard dollar på årets kampanj. Här är valstriderna att hålla ett extra öga på; de kan ge en fingervisning om vem som vinner kampen om kongressen – och därmed över den lagstiftande agendan i världens mäktigaste land. I dag dominerar republikanerna kongressen, och för demokraterna att få kontrollen krävs en nettoökning på tre mandat i representanthuset och fyra mandat i senaten. En demokratisk seger i båda kamrarna hade begränsat Donald Trumps makt avsevärt. Georgia , Michigan och New Hampshire är avgörande platser som Demokraterna måste behålla och där konkurrensen är som hårdast. Demokraterna försöker också att vinna platserna i Maine och North Carolina . Men det finns även andra republikanska fästen som kan skifta sida: Alaska , Iowa , Ohio och Texas. Striden om Texas väntas bli en tydlig symbol för hur valet har avlöpt. Där har ingen demokrat vunnit ett delstatstäckande val sedan 1994. Här behöver demokraterna en nettoökning på minst tre mandat för att få en majoritet. Strategin är att försöka vinna så många mandat som möjligt i en begränsad grupp valkretsar som bedöms vara extra konkurrensutsatta, rapporterar Sky News. Det är distrikt som 2024 hade s må marginaler i president- och kongressvalet.; valkretsar med "delade röster" , alltså där väljarna röstade på olika partier i presidentvalet respektive valet till representanthuset 2024; valkretsar som bytte politisk tillhörighet i valet till representanthuset 2024 och valkretsar utan sittande representant. Demokraten James Talarico ställer upp till senaten i Texas. I en podcast som släpptes under måndagen säger han att han vill samarbeta med Trump på flera områden, rapporterar Fox News. – Som nästa senator för Texas hade jag älskat att jobba med Trump på att faktiskt fullfölja hans politiska projekt, berättar han i podden, rapporterar Fox News. Bland annat vill Talarico samarbeta i bostadsfrågan och sjukvårdsfrågan. Och passar samtidigt på att lyfta fram sina egna hjärtefrågor.
